newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Shaman near new partnership.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Shaman near new partnership.

text.p: Shaman Pharmaceuticals Inc is in "multiple late stage discussions" for potential partners in its diabetes drug program and expects to enter a collaboration before the end of the year, president and chief executive officer Lisa Conte told Reuters.

She also said Shaman expects within two years to have a diabetes product in development based on its ethno-botanical drug discovery approach, which locates compounds in tropical plants around the world. To that end, she said Shaman is seeking a five-year partnership "with a component of committed capital, combined with milestone payments."
She said the financing from such a partnership could also help fund other projects in earlier-stage development.
"The challenge is to pick and manage a partnership so that it allows us to move all our projects as rapidly through clinical development as we can," Conte said.
"And that involves letting go of some of the later-stage projects," she added, referring to the company's practice of outlicensing some international rights to its products.
The company's diabetes drug project aims to offer improved blood glucose-lowering properties.
"A big deficiency of the drugs on the market is the efficacy in lowering (glucose). The agents that are out there now just don't do it well enough," Conte said.
Conte also said Shaman plans to file within the next two to three years a New Drug Application (NDA) with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration for its Provir drug to treat diarrhea.

Provir has been developed as a drug to treat "traveler's diarrhea," or that which often afflicts travelers in developing countries. But Shaman is also exploring uses in treating child diarrhea and diarrhea in AIDS patients, which Conte said could lead to a speedier approval.

"It could be on the market in 12 to 18 months (as a drug for AIDS patients)," said Conte. "Every single AIDS patient is at some point afflicted with chronic diarrhea. It is the most important cause of the wasting syndrome in AIDS patients."

Shaman's other major project, its Virend drug for general herpes in AIDS patents, will enter Phase III clinical trials before year-end, but Shaman is not expected to apply for an NDA until 1998, Conte said. Because of the long development time, she added that Shaman will explore Virend's potential both as a stand-alone treatment and in combination with existing herpes drugs.

"We have to be very realistic about the competition that is well entrenached," she said. "While we are getting it approved, we are also conducting a study to see how much faster patients respond with a combination of drugs."
